counting_rules: Unique API path patterns and implemented method+path operations were recalculated fresh from the live django.urls.get_resolver() output on 2026-09-29 — not copied from any earlier document's numbers.
GET and POST on the same path = 2 operations; GET and PATCH = 2 operations. A path with only one method = 1 operation.
HEAD and OPTIONS are excluded — DRF adds these automatically to every APIView/GenericAPIView; they were never counted as separate operations.
Django Admin (/admin/...) and any static/media route are excluded entirely.
A method only counts as implemented if that HTTP verb is genuinely defined somewhere in the view class's MRO (get/post/put/patch/delete), not merely theoretically routable.

This project has no DELETE endpoint anywhere — every lifecycle transition is a paired POST .../activate/ / .../deactivate/ or an equivalent named action (submit/confirm/issue/approve/post/cancel), never a hard delete.

discrepancies.area: Material Requisitions vs. the client register's 'Requisition Status' field
discrepancies.finding: Task 13A's MaterialRequisition (apps.material_requisitions) is a separate, richer concept — an actual requisition document with material lines and calculated quantities — from the client's own single 'Requisition Status' column on their register (previously mapped to StorePreparation, which deliberately has no such field). MaterialRequisition.status has exactly ONE value (DRAFT) today; the multi-state lifecycle the client's column implies (submitted/fulfilled/etc.) is still unanswered. Do not read Task 13A as having resolved that field — see docs/client-register-field-mapping.md and docs/erp-handoff-open-decisions.md.

docs/api-inventory-current.md (written earlier this session) states no CORS configuration exists anywhere in the codebase. That was true when it was written and is now OUTDATED by a separate, later task in this same session: django-cors-headers is now installed and wired into config/settings/base.py (corsheaders app + CorsMiddleware) and config/settings/local.py now reads CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS from the environment. Both CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS default to EMPTY — nothing is enabled unless a developer's own .env sets them, so a plain single-machine local run is unaffected. This dashboard reflects the CURRENT, code-verified state, not the inventory doc's now-stale claim.

discrepancies.area: Formula approval — intro text vs later sections
discrepancies.finding: docs/frontend-api-handoff.md §14's own opening paragraph says 'no approval... Do not render Approve...' — written before Task 11C added real approval. §14.8c (later in the same document) is the correct, current contract: approve/approval-preview/approval-policy all exist and are implemented. This dashboard follows §14.8c and the live code, not §14's stale opening paragraph.

Every core business-transaction module (customers, products, quotations, sales_orders, formulas, batch_plans, store_preparation, quality, receiving, purchasing) requires expected_version on every mutating call — confirmed directly by searching every app's serializers.py for the literal field. By contrast, apps.catalog (units/categories/materials), apps.companies, apps.stores, apps.suppliers, apps.users and apps.permissions (role management) have ZERO expected_version usage anywhere — confirmed the same way. These administrative/reference-data modules perform unconditional overwrites with no conflict detection. This is a real, current gap, not a dashboard error — flagged per-operation in the Version Token column.

discrepancies.area: Three distinct 'version' concepts on Material Specifications and Formulas
discrepancies.finding: Both resources carry a row's own optimistic-concurrency token, a plain server-side allocation counter (never sent as expected_version), and a child record's own separate concurrency token. docs/frontend-api-handoff.md §9.2/§14.3 document this distinction explicitly after a real bug (Task 09B-3B.1) where the first implementation of MaterialSpecification shipped with NO concurrency token at all, reasoning it was unversioned master-data — fixed the same session. This dashboard keeps the three counters visually separate in every affected operation's detail panel.
